subject: Mid-cycle objective health review — scope pivots & dependency asks
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle objective health review — scope pivots & dependency asks

Team,

Attached is a concise mid-cycle snapshot (midcycle_okr_snapshot.xlsx). I pulled together the latest signal across telemetry, customer feedback, and delivery plans. High-level summary:

- Objective A (Serving reliability): Green -> on track. Incidents down 43% MoM. Continue rollout of hotfix for KV cache edge-case. No scope changes.
- Objective B (Latency & TPS per-dollar): Yellow -> trending behind. Primary cause: model memory pressure + inefficient batching for multi-tenant workloads.
- Objective C (Developer DX / Console rollout): Red -> missed two ship windows; needs rescope.

Asks (owners + dates):
1) Infrastructure (Vivek) — provide a short-term throughput uplift plan (dedicated queue + smaller batch profiles) by EOD Tue 18 Aug. This must include expected p95 latency impact and cost delta.
2) Serving/runtime (Marcus) — validate whether a quantized variant for the 13B family reduces memory enough to enable target batch size; share a test plan and ETA (suggested: prototype by Thu 20 Aug). Attach throughput_estimates.pdf if helpful.
3) Product & DX (Lauren) — propose a scoped launch plan for Console features (reduce to core telemetry + rollout to 2 pilot customers) by Tue 18 Aug so we can hit the QBR milestone.
4) Sales/Customer (Aditya) — coordinate with Acme Health (Priya) about shifting their pilot start by two weeks and capture any SLA commitments; update procurement status on the shared doc.

Decision points I need after these asks: a) approval to formally rescope Objective C for QBR metrics (I will sign off once Lauren shares the trimmed plan), b) permission to allocate a temporary dedicated GPU pool for top-tier customers (Vivek to quantify cost).

I'll run a 30-minute check-in on Wed 19 Aug at 10:00 PT if we have updates; otherwise we'll sync in the leadership slot. Please reply with confirmations and any roadblocks.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Platform & Infra
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- midcycle_okr_snapshot.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle objective health review — scope pivots & dependency asks

Irene — thanks for the summary and the snapshot. Confirming I own ask (1). Quick notes:

- Short-term: we can spin a dedicated queue for the top 10% of tenants within 48 hours (capacity permitting). That will reduce noisy multi-tenant interference and let Marcus's quantization experiment run with less variance.
- Cost: initial back-of-envelope is ~15% incremental infra spend for the short window; will firm up numbers after Marcus's throughput numbers.
- Risk: if traffic spikes beyond forecast, the dedicated pool could still suffer tail latency; will propose a fallback routing rule to route heavy tails to a lower-cost model variant.

I'll put a one-pager in the shared drive and link it here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFG-midcycle-okrs (see "infra-temp-pool-v1"). Planning to have the plan + cost by EOD Tue 18 Aug.

Vivek
Director, Infrastructure

Quick update from serving/runtime side. I'm aligned on the plan and will start the quantization/variant tests this week. Notes:

- Test plan: run 48-hour A/B against a 1% traffic slice for the 13B baseline vs quantized v1; measure p95, memory, and quality deltas on our eval prompts. Prototype ETA: Thu 20 Aug.
- Throughput estimates attached — these assume no other infra mitigations. If Vivek can get the dedicated queue, we should see batch sizes increase 20–30% with a commensurate token-cost reduction.
- Known failure mode: quantization can increase token-level hallucination risk on a few prompt families. We'll add a focused eval suite and a rollback flag.

I'll share the prototype results and link to the hc-run logs in Jira INF-1243 when ready.

Marcus
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Attachments:
- throughput_estimates.pdf
